questions.title: Which bank will the U.S. Treasury sanction over alleged financial ties to Iran during August 31–September 6, 2026?
questions.background: The United States uses financial sanctions to restrict institutions accused of helping Iran access the international financial system.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official U.S. Treasury sanctions announcements and Office of Foreign Assets Control designation records. Resolution Conditions : Identify the bank newly sanctioned during August 31–September 6, 2026, for allegedly facilitating financial transactions for Iran. Resolve when the Treasury publicly announces the designation. Accepted Answer Format : The bank's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: Refined ahead of the Aug 31-Sept 6 window using 2026-08-28/29 reporting (Iran International, Sullivan & Cromwell, AP News, Khaleej Times, Arab News). Following FinCEN's Aug 28 Section 311 proposed rule on Banque Misr UAE (outside the Aug 31-Sept 6 window, with the UAE Central Bank launching an urgent forensic probe on Aug 29), Iran International (Aug 29) confirms two critical targeting points: (1) Turkey's Halkbank already ended its decade-long US criminal case earlier this year via a deal barring Iran business touching the US and Turkish banks are avoiding Iran-linked payments—removing Halkbank (0.02 -> 0); (2) Washington views Dubai and Baghdad—not Beijing—as Iran's primary usable hard-currency corridors, with Iraq pressure focused on policing USD correspondent channels and cutting off Iraqi banks moving money for Iran and its militias. Accordingly, we lift Iraq's most scrutinized state bank Rafidain Bank (0.10 -> 0.11), hold Trade Bank of Iraq (0.045) and Rasheed Bank (0.035), add Iraq's leading vetted private USD-correspondent bank National Bank of Iraq (0.02), and trim Bank of China (0.02 -> 0.015) given repeated reporting of US reluctance to hit major Chinese G-SIBs, keeping total top-5 mass disciplined at 0.225.

questions.title: Which commodity category will record the largest monthly percentage price increase in the FAO Food Price Index for August 2026?
questions.background: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) publishes a monthly index tracking international prices across major food commodity categories.
questions.resolution_criteria: Resolve to the commodity category with the largest percentage price increase from July to August 2026, as reported in the FAO's September 2026 Food Price Index release. Resolution Date: 2026-09-04 Answer with the category name.
questions.current_reasoning: With 20 of 21 August trading days complete as of Friday Aug 28, hard futures data strongly cements Sugar's monthly-average lead. ICE #11 raw sugar surged another +3.58% on Aug 27 to 18.22 c/lb (highest since March 2025, per FXDailyReport), extending its +19.47% MoM gain as of Aug 24 (iGrowNews/Trading Economics) driven by Brazil's 32% ethanol blend hike, El Nino crop fears, and India's 1M-tonne duty-free raw sugar import authorization (which eased Indian retail sugar slightly on Aug 27 but supports international raw sugar demand). By contrast, Vegetable Oils clearly trail (Aug 24 data: Palm Oil +8.57% MoM diluted by Rapeseed -3.41%, Canola -2.98%, Soybeans -0.65%; trimmed 0.075 -> 0.04). Cereals staged a sharp late-August spike (CNBC Aug 28: wheat +12.1% on the week to 784 c/bu on Black Sea disruptions; corn +15.6% in August to 536.5 c/bu on Pro Farmer yield cuts), making Cereals clear #2 (0.08), though wheat was -3.44% MoM through Aug 24 and rice was +1.68%, heavily damping the full-month FAO Cereals average relative to Sugar's sustained double-digit surge. Raising Sugar 0.83 -> 0.86, Dairy and Meat unchanged at 0.01 each.

questions.title: Which Southeast Asian country will declare a state of emergency over wildfire haze between September 1 and September 5, 2026?
questions.background: Seasonal wildfire smoke can cross borders in Southeast Asia, creating public-health risks and prompting emergency government responses.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official national government announcements, corroborated by reliable news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the country whose national authorities announce a formal state of emergency because of wildfire haze between September 1 and September 5, 2026, inclusive. The declaration may cover the entire country or a specific area within it. Air-quality warnings, school closures, or health advisories without a formal emergency declaration do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country’s common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-28/29 haze escalation across both Malaysia and Indonesia reverses yesterday's assumption that Malaysia was easing, narrowing the gap just three days before the Sept 1-5 window. In Malaysia (The Star Aug 28; Malay Mail Aug 29 noon MYT), air quality surged sharply back from just 4 unhealthy stations on Aug 27 to 22 stations nationwide on Aug 28 and FOUR 'very unhealthy' (>200) Sarawak locations on Saturday Aug 29—Lubok Antu (230), Lundu (228), Sri Aman (227), and Serian (204)—plus 8 more unhealthy Sarawak sites as NOAA-20 detected 1,738 hotspots in Kalimantan drifting dense smoke straight north into western Sarawak; combined with Malaysia's direct federal statutory precedent for localized haze States of Emergency (Darurat), Malaysia rebounds sharply 0.37 -> 0.435. Simultaneously, Indonesia's crisis worsened dramatically (The Star/Bernama Aug 28; CNA/Al Jazeera Aug 29): six sites hit HAZARDOUS (ISPU >300), led by an extreme ISPU 835 in Pekanbaru (Riau) and five Central Kalimantan locations (301-456) as Central Kalimantan hotspots jumped 10x to 4,359 and >5M people face direct exposure—keeping Indonesia slight favorite at 0.50 (trimmed from 0.55 given Jakarta's historical reluctance to elevate provincial emergencies to a formal national declaration). Singapore's PSI remains moderate 56-64 (0.03 -> 0.025), northeastern Sarawak near Brunei remains moderate 52-68 (Brunei 0.025 -> 0.02), and Thailand trims 0.015 -> 0.01.

questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?

questions.current_reasoning: Significant 2026-08-28 outbreak expansion update (AP News, Al Jazeera, Arab News, Korea Times Aug 28): DRC Ministry of Health figures published Friday show confirmed Ebola cases climbed to 5,794 with 2,786 deaths (+138 cases since Aug 26) across 60 health zones — and BOTH newly affected health zones, Biena and Manguredjipa, are in North Kivu province, where delayed response efforts have produced a case fatality rate well above the 48% national average. Simultaneously, MSF announced Friday it opened a new emergency treatment center in Beni, North Kivu (122 confirmed cases, 87 deaths, ~69% CFR), calling it one of the hardest-hit areas. Combined with ECDC's Aug 26 finding that North Kivu accounts for 78% of confirmed cases outside Ituri (735 cases, 501 deaths) amid M23 displacement and insecurity, North Kivu strengthens further as the prime candidate for WHO's mid-September surging-cases assessment (0.39 -> 0.47). Meanwhile, frontline Ervebo vaccinations launched Thursday in Kisangani (Tshopo) moving in a ring around Ituri. Haut-Uele remains a serious #2 surge risk (0.27 -> 0.23; ETC collapse and weak tracing), followed by epicenter Ituri (0.18 -> 0.16), Bas-Uele (0.08 -> 0.07), and Tshopo (0.06 -> 0.05), leaving 0.02 residual for other provinces.
